title: De-duplication does not increase term length
statement: Let $t$ be a term, that is, a finite list of literals over the variables $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $t'$ be the term obtained from $t$ by scanning it and keeping each literal only when no literal already kept uses the same variable. Then $t'$ has length at most that of $t$.
hypotheses_covered: t is a term (a finite list of literals over n variables)
replaced:
The de-duplicated term is no longer than the original:
$(\mathrm{dedupTermVar}\,t).\mathrm{length} \le t.\mathrm{length}$.
